subject: Discovery: cost & capacity roadmap — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@mercurypay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2028 10:03 -0400
Subject: Discovery: cost & capacity roadmap — post-call recap and next steps

Jordan — thanks for a productive conversation this morning. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we can align on the smallest set of work that demonstrates ROI quickly.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- High token spend on session-based chat features (customer support and invoices flows).
- Latency spikes during peak batching windows impacting UX (timeouts on mobile requests).
- Internal constraint: Q3 budget guidance is tight; any pilot likely needs to land <$60k initially.
- Compliance: need clear handling for PII in logs and audit trail for finance workflows.

What we heard are your goals:
1) Reduce per-request inference cost by 40–60% within pilot window (3–6 weeks).
2) Keep p95 latency under 350ms for the critical path.
3) Prove a path to predictable monthly run-rate under reserved capacity if unit economics justify it.

Initial technical levers we discussed (high level):
- Batching: session-aware continuous batching for chat to improve GPU utilization.
- KV prefix caching: avoid re-tokenizing repeated prompts and system messages.
- Model selection/quantization: routing higher-volume lower-cost requests to a cheaper quantized variant.
- Dedicated pools vs hosted: trade-offs between unit cost and operational isolation.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) ROI workshop (60 mins) — we’ll run a simple spend model using your 7-day telemetry and show Hosted-optimized vs Dedicated scenarios. (Propose Wed Apr 25, 11:00 AM ET).
2) We’ll send a short telemetry request (sample CSV + ingestion instructions) so our econ team can produce the capacity-estimate.xlsx.
3) Draft two pilot options: (A) Hosted pilot with aggressive caching + batching and (B) Reserved Dedicated pilot with a 3-month commit — we’ll include cost ranges and risk tradeoffs in pilot-options-onepager.pdf.
4) Security/compliance note: I’ll loop in our security lead for a short questionnaire and evidence pack (SOC2 artifacts, audit log samples).

Attachments: [attachment: capacity-estimate.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)], [attachment: redwood-econ-brief.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

If that lines up with your priorities, I’ll lock the ROI workshop and Ben will draft the two-option one-pager for decision.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Discovery: cost & capacity roadmap — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Grace — appreciate the concise recap. Confirming that your notes capture our priorities. A few clarifications from my side:
- Budget: our finance team has flagged a Q3 pilot cap of $60k unless we can show clear monthly run-rate improvement and a near-term payback.
- Workloads: ~1.2M monthly conversational messages in scope for pilot, with a heavy long-tail of 1–3 short messages per session.
- Compliance: PII redaction in logs is a hard requirement; we can share a sample request pattern but not raw logs.

Ben — if we can see a Hosted-optimized scenario that hits ~45% cost reduction using caching and batching assumptions, that will be compelling. If Dedicated gets us to similar economics with a predictable SLA and segregation, procurement will entertain the larger commit.

I can do Wed Apr 25, 11:00 AM ET for the ROI workshop. Please send the telemetry template; I’ll loop procurement if we need contract/PO discussions after the economic readout.

—Jordan
Jordan Ellis

Subject: Re: Discovery: cost & capacity roadmap — post-call recap and next steps

Jordan — good call. I’ll own the pilot-options one-pager and will include two concrete packages:
A) Hosted-optimized pilot (no commit) — leverages continuous batching, KV prefix caching, and a quantized policy for low-cost routes. Expected outcomes: 35–55% token cost reduction (range depends on hit-rate and session length).
B) Dedicated pilot (3-month reserved pool) — pricing anchored to guaranteed throughput with over-provision burst buffer. Expected outcomes: 45–65% cost reduction at higher utilization; better p95 stability.

Request for Jordan: please share the 7-day telemetry snippet (redacted for PII) — columns: timestamp, session_id (hashed), tokens_in, tokens_out, endpoint_type. Grace sent the capacity-estimate.xlsx to start; we’ll run quick sensitivity analysis and return ranges before the workshop.

I’m attaching a brief one-pager that frames the operational tradeoffs and sample cost bands.
Attachment: [attachment: pilot-options-onepager.pdf (pdf, 58KB)]

I’ve added Marcus so he can validate latency/SLO implications on Dedicated sizing.

Thanks — Ben
